A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeltaPhi residual operator learning for PDE solving. Despite the revised title and organization, the methods, experiments, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D can be reliably matched and read.

before.justification: V1 reports original DeltaPhi experiments across regular and irregular PDE domains, resolution generalization, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of test-distribution sensitivity, sampling, interpolation, learned symmetry, additional architectures, and runtime.

M1.justification: V2 adds an optional similarity-weighted importance-sampling procedure in Appendix A.6. Equation (6) also changes the stated retrieval score from one minus cosine similarity to cosine similarity, making maximization consistent with nearest-sample retrieval; this does not establish that the implementation changed. The core residual architecture, default top-K sampling, and Fourier resolution alignment are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate regular Darcy Flow, Navier-Stokes, Irregular Darcy, Pipe Turbulence, Heat Transfer, Composite, and Blood Flow. V2's similarity-based test groups partition existing Darcy data; they do not introduce a new dataset, physical domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix A.9 adds evaluated Transolver and HPM direct-learning baselines alongside their DeltaPhi counterparts on Irregular Darcy. The retrieval-range comparison now reports only FNO on Darcy, whereas v1 included FNO and Resnet on both Darcy and Navier-Stokes. The comparator sets in main Tables 1, 2, and 4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce substantial evaluation procedures: seven test groups defined by nearest-training-sample cosine similarity, a reversed-input diagnostic metric tracked through 1800 epochs, and CPU/GPU retrieval plus end-to-end timing comparisons. These supplement the retained main benchmark protocols; the existing resolutions, model configurations, and default 500-epoch training setup are not generally revised.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of performance across similarity-defined test groups, importance versus fixed-range sampling, Fourier versus bilinear/nearest interpolation, emergence of residual antisymmetry, and computational overhead. Conversely, v1's Figure 6 sensitivity study is narrowed to the FNO/Darcy subset in v2 Table 5, dropping Resnet, Navier-Stokes, and 900-sample coverage there. The existing input, inference-selection, and distance-function ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The same five randomized auxiliary-selection inference evaluations and standard deviation of 5.40649e-5 appear in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 9. V2 adds no training-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain their values, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 7 and 11-16. Examples include Darcy importance-sampling error of 3.22e-2, symmetry loss declining from 2.01 to 3.22e-2, and Transolver errors of 8.54e-3 versus 8.18e-3 with DeltaPhi. These are newly reported comparisons, not cross-version performance gains. V2 also omits Table 3's Resnet numerical rows and much of v1 Figure 6.

T1.justification: V2 introduces an explicit Lipschitz stability condition in Section 3.1, the importance-sampling distribution in Equation (17), and the normalized reversed-input residual metric in Equation (18). These are limited formal additions; neither version supplies a theorem or proof establishing DeltaPhi's generalization advantage. The Fourier alignment mathematics largely restates procedures already documented in v1.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly claim that physical-system stability underpins effective implicit augmentation through residual pairs. V1 emphasized residual-label diversity and empirical generalization without this explicit stability foundation. The central claims of architecture compatibility and improved PDE solving with limited data remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanism discussion with solution-manifold geometry, residual smoothness, learned symmetry, and implicit boundary-condition handling. It recasts modest Navier-Stokes gains as evidence of robustness and emphasizes retrieval-range insensitivity, whereas v1 stressed constrained gains and the importance of choosing K. Limitations now emphasize cosine retrieval in complex dynamics; the model-capacity caveat remains in Section 3.5 rather than disappearing.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project repository address and identifies an RTX 3090 for GPU retrieval timing. Most dataset specifications, model hyperparameters, optimizer settings, batch size, and training hardware guidance are unchanged. Fourier upsampling and downsampling were already described in v1's appendix, so their expanded main-text treatment does not establish a new implementation.

R1.justification: V2 expands the cited operator-learning literature and adds an explicit comparison with Reference Neural Operators, distinguishing residuals between physical states from residuals associated with geometric deformations. Transolver and HPM are also newly positioned and evaluated. The earlier ResMem and other residual-learning comparisons remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and terminology shifts from physical trajectories to physical states. Background and related work are combined, methodology is reorganized around stability, retrieval, architecture, and generalization, and resolution-alignment material moves into the main text. The limitations and conclusion reverse order, and the appendix narrative is substantially expanded and reorganized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is completely redrawn into direct-operator, residual-operator, and retriever panels, and Algorithm 1 is added. V1's Figure 6 becomes a narrower tabular presentation, numerous new experimental tables appear, and retained appendix tables are reformatted and relocated. Table 3 loses its Resnet rows. Figures 2-5 largely retain their underlying visual evidence, with some caption and annotation changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through a clearer architecture diagram, retrieval-equation correction, repository pointer, and targeted experiments addressing distribution sensitivity, interpolation choices, and computational cost. These provide useful evidence beyond v1's aggregate comparisons. The gain is tempered by lost Resnet/Navier-Stokes ablation coverage and stronger interpretations than the evidence establishes: correlation plots do not verify the stated Lipschitz condition, and Table 16's approximately 0.47 ms FNO overhead is about 39% of its 1.20 ms baseline despite being called negligible. Overall, the additions support a limited net quality improvement.
